title_en: Wu et al. v. PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Luzhou Branch et al. — dispute over a marine insurance contract
ruling_gist_en: Liability insurance is a form of property insurance in which the subject matter of insurance is the liability for compensation that the insured shall legally bear to a third party, and the insurer actually pays the compensation for damages that the insured owes to the third party. When a third party dies due to an accident within the scope of coverage under the liability insurance, whether the insurance proceeds paid by the insurer can be deemed as the estate of the third party shall be determined based on the nature of the liability for compensation that the insured shall bear to the third party. It cannot be concluded merely because liability insurance is classified as property insurance that the insurance proceeds under liability insurance belong to the estate of the third party. The death compensation and solatium for mental distress that the insured shall compensate for the death of the third party are compensation to the close relatives of the deceased and do not belong to the estate of the third party. The insurance proceeds paid by the insurer under the liability insurance contract for the above damages shall not be deemed as the estate of the third party.
keywords_en: civil; insurance contract dispute; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Sichuan Province; Hubei Province; natural person; legal person; Insurance Law; Civil Code; whether liability insurance proceeds constitute estate; characterization of death compensation; reversal; ship sinking; crewmember death; liability insurance claims; contract dispute; insurance contract; disputes over insurance contracts for navigable waters, etc.
full_text_en:
Wu et al. v. People's Insurance Company of China, Luzhou Branch et al. — dispute over insurance contract for navigable waters

Ruling Gist

Liability insurance is a form of property insurance in which the subject matter of insurance is the liability for damages that the insured shall bear to a third party according to law, and the insurer actually bears the insured's liability for damages to the third party. When a third party dies due to an accident within the scope of coverage under the liability insurance, whether the insurance proceeds paid by the insurer can be identified as the estate of the third party should be determined based on the nature of the liability for damages that the insured shall bear to the third party. It cannot be concluded that the insurance proceeds under the liability insurance belong to the third party's estate merely because liability insurance is classified as property insurance. The compensation for death, solatium, and other damages that the insured shall pay for the third party's death constitute compensation to the decedent's close relatives and do not belong to the third party's estate. The insurance proceeds paid by the insurer under the liability insurance contract for the above damages should not be identified as the estate of the third party.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2024) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 18

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Wu, female, born June 21, 1937, Han ethnicity, residing in Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Wu Shaojun, lawyer at Sichuan Cijian Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: You Shuangjiang, lawyer at Sichuan Cijian Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Li A, female, born May 15, 1993, Han ethnicity, residing in Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Wu Shaojun, lawyer at Sichuan Cijian Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: You Shuangjiang, lawyer at Sichuan Cijian Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): People's Insurance Company of China, Luzhou Branch. Domicile: Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province.

Representative: Chen Yaling, General Manager of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Xie Wei, lawyer at Sichuan Changsong Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Respondent at Second Instance): Li C, male, born November 7, 1991, Han ethnicity, residing in Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province.

Respondent at Second Instance (Third Party at First Instance): Luzhou Yujiang Shipping Co., Ltd. Domicile: Naxi District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Cheng Lifu, Executive Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Dong Pingfu, lawyer at Sichuan Rongchuang (Luzhou) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Kuang Yalin, lawyer at Sichuan Rongchuang (Luzhou) Law Firm.

The applicants for retrial, Wu and Li A, filed an application with this Court for retrial against the civil judgment (2023) E-Min-Zhong No. 296 rendered by the Hubei High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance), in a dispute over insurance contract for navigable waters with the respondent, People's Insurance Company of China, Luzhou Branch (hereinafter referred to as PICC Luzhou Branch), Li C, and the respondent at second instance, Luzhou Yujiang Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yujiang Company). This Court, by civil ruling (2023) Supreme People's Court Min-Shen No. 1637 dated November 30, 2023, decided to bring this case for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing of this case on January 30, 2024. The agents ad litem of the applicants for retrial Wu and Li A, Wu Shaojun and You Shuangjiang, the agent ad litem of the respondent PICC Luzhou Branch, Xie Wei, the respondent Li C, and the agent ad litem of the respondent at second instance Yujiang Company, Dong Pingfu, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Wu, Li A, and Li C filed a lawsuit with the Wuhan Maritime Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance), requesting: 1. An order that PICC Luzhou Branch pay them insurance compensation of RMB 2,200,000 and overdue interest (among which, for employer's liability insurance, RMB 600,000 per person for death; for hull all risks insurance, RMB 500,000 per person for death; the interest shall be calculated based on the principal of RMB 2,200,000 from October 27, 2021, at the contemporaneous LPR until the date the insurance compensation is fully paid); 2. That PICC Luzhou Branch bear the litigation costs of this case.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

The vessel "Yujiang 66" is a steel dry cargo vessel, formerly named "Guihua 2", with ship identification number CN20034866089. The registered owner of the vessel is Yujiang Company, and the ownership was acquired on February 25, 2021.

On March 12, 2021, Yujiang Company (Party A) and Li B (Party B) entered into a "Vessel Affiliation Operation Agreement", which mainly provided: I. Party B purchased the second-hand damaged vessel "Guihua 2" with its own funds and later fully converted it into the general cargo vessel "Yujiang 66". To obtain the operating permit, Party A was required to meet the regulation of 5,000 gross tonnage, so Party B's affiliated vessel was registered under Party A's name, but in fact Party B owned all the property rights of the vessel. II. The affiliation period was three years, from March 2, 2021, to March 1, 2024. III. Affiliation fee and payment method. IV. Responsibilities and rights of Party A and Party B...

On March 22, Yujiang Company submitted to PICC Luzhou Branch an "Application Form for Inland River Vessel Insurance (2009 Edition) of People's Insurance Company of China", purchasing for the vessel "Yujiang 66" inland river hull all risks insurance, with additional shipowner's liability to crew insurance. The bottom of the application form contained a declaration by the applicant (in bold font): The insurer has provided me with the insurance clauses applicable to this insurance and introduced them in detail, and has given me a clear explanation of the clauses exempting the insurer from liability (including but not limited to liability exemptions, obligations of the applicant and the insured, settlement of claims, other matters, etc.), as well as the payment terms and special terms in this insurance contract. I have fully understood and accepted the above contents, agree to use them as the basis for entering into this insurance contract, and voluntarily apply for this insurance. Yujiang Company affixed its seal at the applicant's signature block. On March 29, the "Inland River Hull All Risks Insurance Policy" (Policy No.: PCEJ20215105000000XXXX) issued by PICC Luzhou Branch stated: Insurance conditions and special terms: 1. For each insurance accident, the insurer shall calculate the indemnity based on the terms and apply a deductible of RMB 5,000 or a deductible rate of 15%, whichever is higher; for total loss accidents, a deductible of 20% applies. 2. Additional shipowner's liability to crew insurance, insured crew members: 6 persons, maximum compensation limit per person: RMB 600,000, with death/disability limit of RMB 500,000 and medical expense limit of RMB 100,000... 4. Crew list: Yu, Zhao A, Zhao B, Zhong A, Li B, Wang... Insurance period: from 00:00 on March 30, 2021, to 24:00 on March 29, 2022. On the same day, the "Employer's Liability Insurance (2015 Edition) Policy" (Policy No.: PZBV20215105000000XXXX) issued by PICC Luzhou Branch stated: Liability name: personal injury liability; limit of liability per person for injury: RMB 600,000. Insurance period: from 00:00 on March 30, 2021, to 24:00 on March 29, 2022. Special terms: 1. The deductible for medical expenses for each accident is 5% of the assessed compensation per person or RMB 200, whichever is higher... 3. Liability limit for each accident: RMB 1,200,000; aggregate liability limit: RMB 3,960,000. The appended employee list named the crew as Yu, Zhao A, Zhao B, Zhong A, Li B, Wang. The insurance premium was paid by Li C and Li B via transfer to Yujiang Company.

On July 23, the vessel "Yujiang 66" suffered a fracture and capsizing accident. On August 4, the 15th Villagers' Group of Xianfeng Village, Jiangbei Town, Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province issued a "Burial Certificate" certifying that Li B and Zhong A died by drowning on July 23, 2021, after a capsizing accident at Xiangjiaba in Shuifu City, Yunnan Province, and were buried on July 29, 2021. On the same day, the Jiangbei Central Health Center of Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, and the Luzhou Municipal Public Security Bureau of Sichuan Province jointly issued a "Resident Death Medical Certificate" certifying the deaths of Li B and Zhong A.

On August 31, the Villagers' Committee of Xianfeng Village, Jiangbei Town, Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province issued a "Relationship Certificate" stating: Li B, citizen identity number 510523196811XXXXXX, eldest son: Li C, citizen identity number 510502199111XXXXXX, second daughter: Li A, citizen identity number 510502199305XXXXXX. The Villagers' Committee of Xiongba Village, Fangshan Town, Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province issued a "Relationship Certificate" stating: Zhong A, citizen identity number 510523197003XXXXXX, mother: Wu, citizen identity number 510523193706XXXXXX, eldest son: Li C, citizen identity number 510502199111XXXXXX, second daughter: Li A, citizen identity number 510502199305XXXXXX.

On the same day, Wu issued a "Power of Attorney for Insurance Claim", authorizing Li A to handle the collection of the insurance proceeds for Zhong A's death. Li C issued a "Power of Attorney for Insurance Claim", authorizing Li A to handle the collection of the insurance proceeds for Li B's death. On September 7, Yujiang Company issued a "Transfer Authorization Letter" and "Power of Attorney", stating that Yujiang Company, as the insured, voluntarily authorized PICC Luzhou Branch to transfer the indemnity to Li A's personal bank account, and fully authorized Li A to handle the procedures for collecting the insurance proceeds for the insurance accidents involving Li B and Zhong A that occurred on July 23, 2021, in the name of Yujiang Company.

On September 10, Yujiang Company issued a "Statement on Ownership of the Vessel Yujiang 66", mainly stating: Li B purchased the second-hand vessel "Guihua 2" with his own funds in 2020, completed the conversion on February 25, 2021, and transferred it to Yujiang Company's name, simultaneously renamed as "Yujiang 66". The registered owner of the vessel is Yujiang Company, but the actual owner is Li B, who operated the vessel independently. Yujiang Company has no property relationship with the vessel "Yujiang 66".

On September 14, Yujiang Company (Party A) and Li C and Li A (Party B) entered into a "Compensation Agreement", mainly stating: Li B's sole-owned vessel "Yujiang 66" was affiliated with Party A, operated and crewed independently by the owner Li B. Party A, entrusted by the owner Li B and in Party A's name, purchased hull all risks insurance and employer's liability insurance for "Yujiang 66" from PICC Luzhou Branch. The compensation obtained from PICC Luzhou Branch belonged to the owner Li B and had nothing to do with Party A. Party A issued a "Claim Authorization Letter" to Party B, allowing Party B to claim against PICC Luzhou Branch. The death compensation for Li B paid by PICC Luzhou Branch belonged to Party B. Based on the wage standard provided by Party B (Class 1 Second Mate salary: RMB 5,500/month) and the maximum compensation for crew death stipulated in the hull all risks insurance and employer's liability insurance for "Yujiang 66", Party A agreed that the total lump-sum payment of RMB 1,137,260 for Li B's death compensation and funeral subsidy paid by PICC Luzhou Branch would be entirely handled by Party B, but the final compensation amount would be based on the actual amount paid by PICC Luzhou Branch. On the same day, Yujiang Company (Party A) and Li C, Li A, and Wu (Party B) entered into a "Compensation Agreement", mainly stating: Li B's sole-owned vessel "Yujiang 66" was affiliated with Party A, operated and crewed independently by the owner Li B. Party A, entrusted by the owner Li B and in Party A's name, purchased hull all risks insurance and employer's liability insurance for "Yujiang 66" from PICC Luzhou Branch. The compensation obtained from PICC Luzhou Branch belonged to the owner Li B and had nothing to do with Party A. Party A issued a "Claim Authorization Letter" to Party B, allowing Party B to claim against PICC Luzhou Branch. The death compensation for Zhong A paid by PICC Luzhou Branch belonged to Party B. Based on the wage standard provided by Party B (seaman salary: RMB 4,200/month) and the maximum compensation for crew death stipulated in the hull all risks insurance and employer's liability insurance for "Yujiang 66", Party A agreed that the total lump-sum payment of RMB 1,045,260 for Zhong A's death compensation and funeral subsidy paid by PICC Luzhou Branch would be entirely handled by Party B, but the final compensation amount would be based on the actual amount paid by PICC Luzhou Branch.

On June 2, 2022, the Zhaotong Local Maritime Safety Administration of Yunnan Province issued an "Investigation Report", mainly stating: I. Vessel particulars... IV. Crew manning and watchkeeping. The "Yujiang 66" was issued a "Minimum Safe Manning Certificate for Inland River Vessels" by the Luzhou Maritime Safety Administration of the People's Republic of China, with a minimum manning of 4 persons, including 1 Class 1 Captain, 1 Class 1 Second Mate, 1 Class 2 Engineer, and 1 ordinary seaman. During the berthing period, the actual personnel on board and the watchkeepers of "Yujiang 66" were: Class 1 Captain Li D, Class 1 Second Mate Li B (certificate number 510523196811XXXXXX, issued by Luzhou Municipal Transportation Bureau of Sichuan Province on August 25, 2017, valid until August 25, 2022), and other persons Zhong A, Zhong B... XIII. Cause analysis. (1) Direct cause: During past operations, the vessel "Yujiang 66" had been overloaded and used a poor loading method of concentrated midship loading for a long time, causing deformation or other possible structural damage to the hull, reducing the overall strength of the vessel. Combined with the identification and investigation analysis of "Yujiang 66" issued by the Chongqing Branch of China Classification Society, based on the structural strength recalculation results of the vessel under the loading condition at the time of the accident, it can be seen that due to concentrated midship loading, the vessel was in an abnormal "sagging" poor stress condition. Under this condition, the overall strength of the vessel was insufficient. Under external forces, the local stress concentration exceeded the ultimate strength of the vessel's material, causing structural instability and deformation. The insufficient overall strength of the vessel was the direct cause of the overall fracture and sinking of the vessel. (2) Indirect causes: 1. Li B, the actual controller, manager, and crew member of the vessel, seriously failed in his responsibility for daily safety management of the vessel, did not fulfill his safety management duties, prioritized profits over safety, had an extremely weak safety awareness, did not regularly inspect, rectify, or eliminate hazards, did not take the safety hazards that could lead to major accidents pointed out by the captain and others seriously during operations, allowed the vessel to be loaded in a concentrated manner for a long time and engaged in serious overloading, and failed to take timely action after learning of hull deformation. 2. Yujiang Company's daily safety management was inadequate. 3. The captain had a weak safety awareness. XIV. Accident responsibility determination. (1) Li B, the actual controller of "Yujiang 66", bore primary responsibility for the accident, while Yujiang Company's inadequate management and the captain's failure to perform duties bore secondary responsibility. (2) The fractured bow of "Yujiang 66" struck the superstructure at the stern of "Jinjiang 5", causing serious damage. "Yujiang 66" bore full responsibility...

On the same day, the Zhaotong Local Maritime Safety Administration of Yunnan Province issued a "Conclusion Report" stating: Time of accident: 1143 hours on July 23, 2021. Location: Anchorage at 380 Dam Transfer Terminal, Shuifu City. Type of accident: sinking accident. Name of involved vessel: "Yujiang 66". Owner/operator of involved vessel: Li B. Brief description: At approximately 1445 hours on July 22, 2021, "Yujiang 66" arrived at No. 10 mooring dolphin at Shuifu 380 Dam Transfer Terminal and berthed, awaiting unloading. At 1140 hours on the 23rd, the vessel "Jiaotou 1" proceeded upstream along the anchorage, returning to the water intake of the Upper Gorge Water Plant. At 1142 hours 34 seconds, the work vessel passed the incident waters at a safe speed and safe distance. Ripples were visible at the stern of the berthed vessels, and a slight external force acted on the berthed vessels. At 1143 hours 24 seconds on the 23rd, the vessel "Yujiang 66" suddenly fractured, splitting instantly into two sections and sinking rapidly. Subsequently, the bow and stern of "Yujiang 66" tilted upward. At 43 minutes 50 seconds, the bow and stern stood upright in the water and slowly inclined toward the middle. At 44 minutes 12 seconds, the stern floated upward and struck the part of the bow above the water surface. The bow floated upward, pushing the stern to drift toward the center of the river. At 44 minutes 44 seconds, the stern and bow separated, and the stern continued drifting toward the center of the river. The bow, buoyed by buoyancy, suddenly floated upward from the water and leaped up, striking the superstructure at the stern of "Jinjiang 5". At the same time, the bow and "Jinjiang 5" drifted toward the center of the river. At 45 minutes 12 seconds, the mooring line of "Jinjiang 5" came under tension, and the vessel stopped drifting. After the accident, all four persons on board "Yujiang 66" fell into the water; one was rescued, and three went missing. The cause of the accident and the attribution of responsibility were consistent with those recorded in the Investigation Report.

It was also found that on August 10, 2021, the Luzhou Local Maritime Safety Administration issued a "Statement on the Training and Examination of Zhong A" stating: Zhong A, female, ID number: 510523197003XXXXXX, from Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province. From July 9 to 12, 2021, she participated in the basic safety education and training for inland river vessel crew organized by the Jiangyang District Shunfeng Crew Training Company of Luzhou City and obtained a training qualification certificate. On July 20, 2021, she participated in the basic safety examination for inland river vessel crew organized by the Luzhou Local Maritime Safety Administration. The examination results were announced on August 6, 2021, and she passed.

On September 14, 2021, an outsider, Huang, filed an application for pre-litigation preservation of property with the court of first instance, requesting the freezing of RMB 3,200,000 in bank deposits of Wu, Li C, and Li A, or the seizure, freezing, or attachment of other property of equivalent value. The court of first instance, in accordance with the law, issued a civil ruling (2021) E 72 Cai Bao No. 34, granting Huang's application for pre-litigation preservation of property, and on September 24, 2021, served an assistance enforcement notice on PICC Luzhou Branch, freezing RMB 3,200,000 of the insurance proceeds payable to Wu, Li C, and Li A. On the same day, outsiders Liu and Hu filed an application for pre-litigation preservation of property with the court of first instance, requesting the freezing of RMB 1,000,000 in bank deposits under the names of Wu, Li C, and Li A, or the seizure, freezing, or attachment of other property of equivalent value. The court of first instance, in accordance with the law, issued a civil ruling (2021) E 72 Cai Bao No. 35, granting Liu and Hu's application for pre-litigation preservation of property, and on September 24, 2021, served an assistance enforcement notice on PICC Luzhou Branch, freezing RMB 1,000,000 of the insurance proceeds payable to Wu, Li C, and Li A. During the period of pre-litigation preservation, Wu and Li A submitted a written "Statement of Waiver of Inheritance Rights" to the court of first instance, stating: 1. We voluntarily waive the right to inherit the estates of Li B and Zhong A; 2. The waiver of inheritance rights is our voluntary act, and we understand the legal consequences of waiving inheritance rights.

On December 13, 2021, non-party Zhang filed an application for pre-litigation property preservation with the Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou, Sichuan Province, requesting the seizure and freezing of insurance claim payments to be made by PICC Luzhou Branch to Wu, Li A, Li B, and Yujiang Company within the value of 440,000 yuan. The Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou, Sichuan Province issued Civil Ruling (2021) Chuan 0502 Cai Bao No. 320, granting Zhang's application for pre-litigation property preservation. On December 15, 2021, it served an Assistance Enforcement Notice on PICC Luzhou Branch, freezing 440,000 yuan of the insurance claim payments that PICC Luzhou Branch was to pay to Wu, Li A, Li B, and Yujiang Company.

On January 12, 2022, non-parties Liu and Cheng filed an application for pre-litigation property preservation with the Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou, Sichuan Province, requesting the freezing of the insurance claim payments payable to Li A and Li B at PICC Luzhou Branch within the value of 700,000 yuan. The Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou, Sichuan Province issued Civil Ruling (2022) Chuan 0502 Cai Bao No. 7, granting the application for pre-litigation property preservation by Liu and Cheng. On January 14, 2022, it served an Assistance Enforcement Notice on PICC Luzhou Branch, freezing 700,000 yuan of the insurance claim payments that PICC Luzhou Branch was to pay to Wu, Li A, and Li B.

For the year 2022, the per capita disposable income of urban residents in Hubei Province for the preceding year was 37,601 yuan per year, the per capita living consumption expenditure of urban residents for the preceding year was 26,422 yuan, and the average annual wage of workers in the transportation industry for the preceding year was 76,200 yuan.

It was further ascertained that Article 4, Paragraph (4) of the Insurance Liability section of the People's Insurance Company of China Inland River Vessel Insurance Clauses (2009 Edition) includes capsizing and sinking caused by accidents. Article 6 of the Exclusions section states that unseaworthiness of the insured vessel includes improper manning, technical condition, navigation area, or use not in compliance with navigation regulations, or improper cargo loading.

The court of first instance held that this case is a dispute over an insurance contract for sea-connected waters. The issues in dispute are: First, whether the insurance claim payments involved in the case constitute the estate of the deceased Li C and Zhong A, and whether Wu and Li B are proper plaintiffs; Second, whether Li A has the right to bring an action on behalf of Yujiang Company to claim insurance compensation from PICC Luzhou Branch; Third, whether the accident involved constitutes an insured event, and whether PICC Luzhou Branch should compensate; Fourth, if PICC Luzhou Branch should compensate, whether a proportional allocation of liability should be made and how the amount of compensation should be determined.

First, regarding the issue of whether the insurance claim payments involved constitute the estate of the deceased Li C and Zhong A, and whether Wu and Li B are proper plaintiffs. PICC Luzhou Branch argued that the insurance claim payments involved belong to property insurance, and Wu and Li B voluntarily waived their inheritance rights to the estates of Li C and Zhong A in written statements, so Wu and Li B are not proper plaintiffs. Article 2 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Insurance Proceeds Can Be Treated as the Estate of the Insured (March 24, 1988) clearly stipulates that property insurance is different from life insurance. There is no issue of designating a beneficiary in property insurance, so property insurance proceeds belong to the estate of the insured.

The inland river vessel all risks insurance with additional shipowner-to-crew liability insurance and employer-to-employee liability insurance involved in this case constitute property insurance, and the insurance claim payments belong to the estate. Wu, being the mother of the deceased Zhong A, and Li B, being the daughter of the deceased Li C, both brought the lawsuit based on their status as first-order heirs; their right of action has a legal basis, and they are proper plaintiffs. However, after Wu and Li B made written statements waiving inheritance, their claim requesting the insurance company to pay the insurance claim payments to them lacks legal basis, and the court of first instance did not protect this claim.

Second, regarding the issue of whether Li A has the right to bring an action on behalf of Yujiang Company to claim insurance compensation from PICC Luzhou Branch. Li A and other close relatives of the deceased Li C and Zhong A entered into a Compensation Agreement with Yujiang Company on September 14, 2021, under which Yujiang Company agreed to compensate for the losses arising from the deaths of Li C and Zhong A in the amounts of 1,137,260 yuan and 1,045,260 yuan, respectively. Yujiang Company's liability for compensation has been determined. Article 65, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Insurance Law) provides that where an insured under liability insurance causes harm to a third party, and the insured's liability to compensate the third party is determined, upon the insured's request, the insurer shall directly compensate the third party with the insurance proceeds. During the trial at first instance, Yujiang Company consented to Li A directly claiming the insurance compensation from PICC Luzhou Branch. Therefore, Li A's claim requesting PICC Luzhou Branch to directly compensate him has a legal basis and was protected by the court of first instance.

Third, regarding the issue of whether the accident involved constitutes an insured event and whether PICC Luzhou Branch should compensate. PICC Luzhou Branch argued that the deceased Li C was the actual owner and operator of the vessel "Yujiang 66" and was not a crew member under the shipowner-to-crew liability insurance nor an employee under the employer-to-employee liability insurance; that is, Li C was not a protected person under the shipowner-to-crew liability insurance and employer-to-employee liability insurance, and the "Yujiang 66" vessel was unseaworthy at the time of the accident, falling under the exclusions of PICC Luzhou Branch. The court of first instance held that, although it could be determined from the Investigation Report and the effective Civil Judgment (2021) E 72 Min Chu No. 802 that Li C was the actual owner of the "Yujiang 66" vessel, the Investigation Report also recorded that Li C was a certified crew member serving as chief officer on the "Yujiang 66". The insurance policy issued by PICC Luzhou Branch also clearly listed Li C and Zhong A in the crew list and employee list. The agreement between Yujiang Company and PICC Luzhou Branch to cover the actual shipowner working on board as a crew member did not violate legal provisions. The court of first instance did not accept this defense by PICC Luzhou Branch. Zhong A participated in and passed the basic safety examination for inland river vessel crew organized by the Luzhou Local Maritime Safety Administration on July 20, 2021; Zhong A was a crew member. The insurance policy issued by PICC Luzhou Branch stated that the insurance contract relationship in this case was governed by the Inland River Vessel Insurance Clauses (2009 Edition). Article 6 of those Clauses defines unseaworthiness of the insured vessel as: improper manning, technical condition, navigation area, or use not in compliance with navigation regulations, or improper cargo loading. The Investigation Report, in its analysis of the cause of the accident, analyzed the direct cause as: during past operations, the "Yujiang 66" vessel, due to overloading and long-term use of poor loading methods concentrating cargo amidships, caused deformation of the hull structure or other possible structural damage, leading to a reduction in the vessel's overall strength... The Investigation Report only determined that the "Yujiang 66" vessel may have had improper cargo loading during "past operations." PICC Luzhou Branch did not submit sufficient and valid evidence to prove that the vessel was unseaworthy on the voyage involved in the accident. Therefore, the court of first instance did not accept this defense by PICC Luzhou Branch. The accident occurred on July 23, 2021, during the insurance period. The sinking of the vessel constitutes an insured event under the inland river vessel all risks insurance. The crew members on board, Li C and Zhong A, died as a result of the accident, and PICC Luzhou Branch should compensate according to law and the contract.

Fourth, regarding the issue of whether a proportional allocation of liability should be made and how the amount of compensation should be determined if PICC Luzhou Branch should compensate. PICC Luzhou Branch argued that even if the court determined that the accident falls within the insurance coverage, under the additional shipowner-to-crew liability insurance, it was entitled to deduct a 15% deductible according to the special terms of the insurance contract involved. Li A argued that the shipowner-to-crew liability insurance is an additional insurance to the inland river vessel all risks insurance; if PICC Luzhou Branch did not clearly explain and draw attention to it, the main insurance clauses could not automatically apply. The fact that PICC Luzhou Branch could not even reasonably explain the improper loading provisions until trial also indicated that it had not given detailed explanations and warnings to Yujiang Company, and therefore the clause was invalid. The court of first instance held that the content of the applicant's declaration in the insurance application form was bolded and highlighted, serving a certain reminder function. Yujiang Company affixed its seal under "Applicant's Signature" and paid the insurance premium in the amount stated in the application form, indicating that Yujiang Company should have read the contents of the application form. According to Article 13, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (II), "If an insured signs, seals, or otherwise confirms on the relevant document that the insurer has fulfilled the obligation of clear explanation that complies with the requirements of Article 11, Paragraph 2 of this Interpretation, it shall be deemed that the insurer has fulfilled that obligation, unless there is other evidence proving that the insurer did not fulfill the obligation of clear explanation." The court of first instance determined that PICC Luzhou Branch had fulfilled its obligation of explanation and warning and had the right to apply the insurance clauses and deduct the absolute deductible for the additional insurance.

As for the losses arising from the deaths of Li C and Zhong A, calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases, the court of first instance calculated: 1. For Li C: death compensation of 752,020 yuan (37,601 yuan/year x 20 years), funeral expenses of 38,100 yuan (76,200 yuan/year / 12 months x 6 months), and solatium of 50,000 yuan, totaling 840,120 yuan; 2. For Zhong A: death compensation of 752,020 yuan (37,601 yuan/year x 20 years), funeral expenses of 38,100 yuan (76,200 yuan/year / 12 months x 6 months), dependent living expenses of 132,110 yuan (26,422 yuan/year x 5 years), and solatium of 50,000 yuan, totaling 972,230 yuan. Li A claimed that PICC Luzhou Branch should pay him insurance compensation of 2.2 million yuan according to the compensation limit. PICC Luzhou Branch argued that the two insurance policies were liability insurance and a proportional allocation of liability should be made, and the shipowner-to-crew liability insurance stipulated an absolute deductible of 15% or 5,000 yuan per accident, entitling PICC Luzhou Branch to reduce the compensation amount accordingly. The court of first instance held that although the Investigation Report and the Conclusion stated that Li C bore primary responsibility for the accident, and Yujiang Company and the captain Li D bore secondary responsibility, the Investigation Report also stated that Captain Li D had alerted Li C to the hazards, and Captain Li D had no fault regarding the occurrence of the accident and should not bear responsibility. Li C actually controlled the "Yujiang 66" vessel and did not follow reasonable suggestions to repair the vessel, constituting gross negligence. The court of first instance partially supported PICC Luzhou Branch's defense that it was entitled to a proportional allocation of liability. Similarly, there was no evidence proving that Zhong A should bear responsibility for the accident, and PICC Luzhou Branch had no right to claim a proportional allocation of liability for the losses arising from Zhong A's death. Considering the circumstances of the case, the court of first instance determined that Li C bore 55% of the accident liability, Yujiang Company bore 45%, and Captain Li D and Zhong A bore no liability. Therefore, Yujiang Company should compensate Li A for losses from Li C's death in the amount of 378,054 yuan (840,120 yuan x 45%) and for losses from Zhong A's death in the amount of 972,230 yuan. Under the shipowner-to-crew liability insurance, deducting a 15% absolute deductible, PICC Luzhou Branch should pay Li A losses from Li C's death in the amount of 321,345.9 yuan (378,054 yuan x 85%) and losses from Zhong A's death in the amount of 500,000 yuan (972,230 yuan after a 15% deductible equals 826,395.5 yuan, exceeding the death/disability limit of 500,000 yuan). Under the employer-to-employee liability insurance, PICC Luzhou Branch should also separately pay Li A losses from Li C's death in the amount of 56,708.1 yuan (378,054 yuan - 321,345.9 yuan) and losses from Zhong A's death in the amount of 472,230 yuan (972,230 yuan - 500,000 yuan). Li A also claimed overdue interest. PICC Luzhou Branch argued that when Yujiang Company requested compensation, the maritime authority had not yet issued an Accident Liability Determination for the accident, and the insurance compensation payable had been frozen by judicial measures by the court of first instance and the Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou, Sichuan Province, so there was no overdue payment. This defense had a factual basis and was supported by the court of first instance. Li A's claim for overdue interest from PICC Luzhou Branch lacked factual and legal basis and was not protected by the court of first instance.

In summary, PICC Luzhou Branch should pay Li A insurance compensation of 1,350,284 yuan. Pursuant to Article 65, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law, Article 67, Paragraph 1 and Article 145 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: 1. PICC Luzhou Branch shall pay Li A insurance compensation of 1,350,284 yuan in a lump sum within ten days from the effective date of the judgment; 2. The other claims of Wu, Li B, and Li A were dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of 24,400 yuan was borne by Wu, Li B, and Li A in the amount of 9,424 yuan, and by PICC Luzhou Branch in the amount of 14,976 yuan.

Wu and Li B, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, requesting: 1. The first-instance judgment (2022) E 72 Min Chu No. 743 be set aside with respect to item 1, and amended to read: "PICC Luzhou Branch shall pay insurance compensation of 1,350,284 yuan in a lump sum to Wu, Li B, and Li A within ten days from the effective date of this judgment"; 2. The appeal fee and the first-instance litigation costs be borne by PICC Luzhou Branch.

PICC Luzhou Branch appealed, requesting: 1. The first-instance judgment (2022) E 72 Min Chu No. 743 be set aside, and PICC Luzhou Branch not be ordered to pay insurance compensation, i.e., Li A's claim against PICC Luzhou Branch be dismissed; 2. The first- and second-instance case acceptance fees be borne by Li A and Yujiang Company.

The court of second instance, after trial, held that this case is a dispute over an insurance contract for sea-connected waters. Based on the arguments of all parties and the facts found, the issues in dispute in this appeal were summarized as: First, whether the insurance claim payments involved constitute estate; Second, whether the accident involved falls within the insurance coverage and whether it falls under exclusions; Third, the proportional allocation of liability and related issues.

1. Whether the insurance claim payments involved constitute estate

Although the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Insurance Proceeds Can Be Treated as the Estate of the Insured had ceased to be effective on January 1, 2021, the case involves inland river vessel all risks insurance and shipowner-to-crew liability insurance. Even if the said Reply is no longer effective, the insurance involved is property insurance, so the insurance claim payments involved should fall within the category of estate. Wu, the mother of the deceased Zhong A, and Li B, the daughter of the deceased Li C, made written statements waiving inheritance. After such waiver, their claim requesting the insurance company to pay the insurance claim payments to them lacks legal basis, and the court of second instance did not support their appeal grounds.

2. Whether the accident involved falls within the insurance coverage and whether it falls under exclusions

First, although Li C was the actual owner of the "Yujiang 66" vessel, the Investigation Report involved also recorded that Li C was a certified crew member serving as chief officer on the "Yujiang 66". Zhong A participated in and passed the basic safety examination for inland river vessel crew organized by the Luzhou Local Maritime Safety Administration on July 20, 2021; Zhong A was a crew member. The insurance policy issued by PICC Luzhou Branch also listed a crew list and an employee list, which included Li C and Zhong A. The agreement between Yujiang Company and PICC Luzhou Branch to cover the actual shipowner working on board as a crew member did not violate legal provisions. The accident involved falls within the insurance coverage. PICC Luzhou Branch's appeal ground that Li C was not a protected person under the Shipowner-to-Crew Liability Insurance and Employer Liability Insurance could not be established, and the court of second instance did not support it.

Second, the Inland River Vessel Insurance Clauses (2009 Edition) apply to this case. Article 6 of those Clauses provides that unseaworthiness (or unseaworthiness for towing) of the insured vessel includes improper manning, technical condition, navigation area, or use not in compliance with navigation (towing) regulations, or improper cargo loading. The Investigation Report involved, in its analysis of the direct cause of the accident, stated: "During past operations, the 'Yujiang 66' vessel, due to overloading and long-term use of poor loading methods concentrating cargo amidships, caused deformation of the hull structure or other possible structural damage, leading to a reduction in the vessel's overall strength... Due to concentrated amidships loading, the vessel was in an abnormal 'sagging' and poor stress condition, under which the overall strength of the vessel was insufficient." That is, the Investigation Report only determined that the "Yujiang 66" vessel may have had improper cargo loading during "past operations" causing a reduction in overall strength, but did not determine that the vessel was unseaworthy on the present voyage. PICC Luzhou Branch's claim that the vessel involved was unseaworthy lacks evidence, and it should bear the adverse consequences of failing to meet its burden of proof.

Third, regarding the manning of the vessel involved, the minimum manning requirement for the vessel was 4 persons: one Class 1 captain, one Class 1 second officer, one Class 2 engineer, and one ordinary crew member. The actual number of persons on board was 4: Captain Li D (Class 1), Second Officer Li C (Class 1), crew member Zhong A, and another person Zhong B. This does not constitute unseaworthiness due to improper manning. Therefore, PICC Luzhou Branch's appeal grounds that the vessel was unseaworthy at the time of the accident, falling under exclusions, lack factual basis, and the court of second instance did not support them.

3. Proportional allocation of liability and related issues

The Investigation Report and Conclusion involved determined the accident liability: Li C, the actual controller (manager/operator, serving as second officer) of the "Yujiang 66", bore primary responsibility; Yujiang Company's inadequate management and the captain's inadequate performance of duties bore secondary responsibility. Li C actually controlled and operated the "Yujiang 66" vessel and did not follow reasonable suggestions to repair the vessel, constituting gross negligence. However, the Investigation Report also stated that Captain Li D had alerted Li C to the hazards, so Captain Li D had no fault regarding the occurrence of the accident and should not bear responsibility. The existing evidence cannot prove that crew member Zhong A should bear responsibility for the accident. PICC Luzhou Branch's appeal ground for proportional allocation of liability for the losses arising from Zhong A's death cannot be established, and the court of second instance did not support it. Considering the accident process, cause analysis, and the circumstances of the case, the first instance court's determination that Li C bore 55% of the accident liability, Yujiang Company bore 45%, and Captain Li D and Zhong A bore no liability was not improper.

In summary, the appeal requests of Wu, Li B, and PICC Luzhou Branch all fail and should be dismissed. Although the first-instance judgment's citation of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Insurance Proceeds Can Be Treated as the Estate of the Insured was improper, it did not affect the substantive handling of the case, and the judgment should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 177, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: the appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed. The second-instance case acceptance fee of 16,953 yuan was borne by Wu and Li B in the amount of 8,476.5 yuan, and by PICC Luzhou Branch in the amount of 8,476.5 yuan.

Wu and Li B applied to this Court for retrial, stating:

1. The insurance policies involved in this case are both liability insurance, and the subject entitled to claim compensation should be determined in accordance with the provisions on liability insurance. The relevant insurance proceeds should not be considered as the inheritance of Li Mouhua and Zhong Mouqun. The Employer's Liability Insurance Policy (2015 Version) and the Inland Vessel All Risks Insurance Policy (Shipowner's Liability to Crew) involved in this case are both liability insurance, with the policyholder and insured being Yujiang Company. According to Article 65 of the Insurance Law, the insurance in dispute in this case is not a personal insurance taken out by Li Mouhua and Zhong Mouqun for themselves, nor is it a personal accident insurance taken out by Yujiang Company for Li Mouhua and Zhong Mouqun. Rather, it is a liability insurance taken out by Yujiang Company, as the registered owner of the vessel, to mitigate its own liability for compensation, with the purpose of substituting its liability for compensation with insurance claim payments. Therefore, the insurance proceeds in this case do not constitute inheritance, and should be obtained by Wu Moulong, Li Moumei, and Li Mou, the close relatives of Li Mouhua and Zhong Mouqun.

2. The insurance proceeds in this case do not meet the definition of inheritance under the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Code). Article 1122 of the Civil Code provides: "Inheritance is the lawful property owned by a natural person at the time of his or her death." The insurance proceeds in this case are not the personal property left by Li Mouhua and Zhong Mouqun at the time of their death, but are payments made by the insurer on behalf of the insured, Yujiang Company, based on legal provisions or contractual agreements, and thus do not meet the definition of inheritance under the Civil Code.

3. The Insurance Law only stipulates the circumstances under which insurance proceeds are considered the inheritance of the insured in the chapter on personal insurance contracts, which does not apply to this case. According to Article 95 of the Insurance Law, insurance business is divided into personal insurance and property insurance, as well as other business related to insurance. An insurer shall not concurrently operate personal insurance and property insurance businesses. Property loss insurance and liability insurance are both types of property insurance business, not personal insurance business. From the perspective of the types of insurance underwritten, the employer's liability insurance and shipowner's liability to crew insurance involved in this case are both liability insurance, with the subject matter being the insured's liability to third parties. Therefore, the insurance in this case does not constitute personal insurance. Furthermore, as mentioned above, an insurer cannot concurrently operate property and personal insurance businesses. The fact that the insurer in this case is "People's Insurance Company of China, Luzhou Branch" also indicates that the insurance involved is a property insurance contract. The provisions of Article 42 of the Insurance Law apply only to personal insurance contracts, not to property insurance contracts. Therefore, the insurance proceeds in this case cannot be determined as inheritance under Article 42 of the Insurance Law. Additionally, the policyholder and insured under both insurance contracts in this case are Yujiang Company, not Li Mouhua and Zhong Mouqun. This fact also does not align with the circumstances under which insurance proceeds are deemed inheritance as stipulated in Article 42 of the Insurance Law.

4. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Insurance Proceeds Can Be Considered as the Insured's Inheritance does not apply to this case. First, this Reply was issued on March 24, 1988, when the category of liability insurance had not yet emerged. Therefore, the Reply does not address circumstances involving liability insurance. Second, the circumstances addressed in the Reply are clearly different from those in this case. In the Reply, the driver insured his own vehicle loss and personal injury, whereas in this case, Yujiang Company insured its liability to its employees and crew. The Reply cannot be directly applied to this case. Third, the subject matter of insurance in the Reply is property owned by the policyholder. Even if insurance had not been taken out, such property would still be treated as inheritance. After insurance is taken out, once an insured event occurs, the insurance proceeds should be treated as a substitute for the insured property and handled as inheritance. However, in this case, when the insurance was taken out, it was not yet known whether Yujiang Company, as the insured, would incur liability to a third party, and there was no possibility of property being converted into inheritance.

5. By comparison with other relevant provisions, the insurance proceeds in this case likewise do not constitute inheritance. According to Article 1213 of the Civil Code, where damage is caused by a motor vehicle accident and the motor vehicle is at fault, compensation shall first be paid by the insurer of the compulsory motor vehicle insurance within the liability limit of the compulsory insurance; any shortfall shall be compensated by the insurer of the commercial motor vehicle insurance in accordance with the insurance contract; and any remaining shortfall or where no commercial motor vehicle insurance has been taken out, compensation shall be paid by the tortfeasor. From the above provision, it can be seen that liability insurance is a mechanism whereby the insurer assumes the liability for compensation on behalf of the party liable, and the nature of the insurance proceeds involved is equivalent to the compensation for death payable by the party liable. According to the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Compensation for Air Crash Death Can Be Treated as Inheritance ( [2004] Min Yi Ta Zi No. 26), compensation for air crash death should not be treated as inheritance, and the corresponding insurance proceeds should be handled similarly.

6. Wu Moulong, Li Mou, and Li Moumei entered into a compensation agreement with Yujiang Company, stipulating that Wu Moulong, Li Mou, and Li Moumei would directly request payment of insurance proceeds from the insurer. According to the provisions of the Insurance Law, Wu Moulong, Li Mou, and Li Moumei may directly claim compensation from the insurance company.

In summary, the insurance proceeds in this case do not constitute inheritance, and Wu Moulong and Li Moumei have the right to assert claims regarding such proceeds. The first-instance and second-instance judgments erred in the application of law and should be corrected according to law. Request: 1. Set aside the first-instance and second-instance judgments, and amend the judgment to order PICC Luzhou Branch to pay insurance proceeds of RMB 1,350,284 to Wu Moulong, Li Moumei, and Li Mou. 2. The litigation costs of the first and second instances shall be borne by PICC Luzhou Branch.

The respondent, PICC Luzhou Branch, argued in defense that the second-instance judgment correctly found the facts and applied the law. First, the insurance policies involved in this case are both liability insurance, which is property insurance in nature. There is no issue of designating a beneficiary for property insurance, so the insurance proceeds arising from property insurance should fall within the scope of inheritance of the insured. Since Wu Moulong and Li Moumei have renounced their inheritance in writing, the original judgment's determination that Li Mou should receive the insurance proceeds was appropriate. Second, the litigation costs of the second instance should not be borne by PICC Luzhou Branch. In the first instance, the subject matter of Wu Moulong and Li Moumei's claim was RMB 2.2 million. On the basis of determining that PICC Luzhou Branch should bear RMB 1.35 million, the original judgment's allocation of first-instance litigation costs proportionally was appropriate. As for the additional facts and reasons submitted by Wu Moulong and Li Moumei, the People's Court shall review them according to law.

The respondent, Li Mou, agreed with the requests of the reapplicants, Wu Moulong and Li Moumei.

The appellee in the second instance, Yujiang Company, stated that the second instance correctly found the facts and applied the law. Wu Moulong and Li Moumei are not the beneficiaries of the liability insurance. The original trial court's direct judgment ordering PICC Luzhou Branch to pay Wu Moulong and Li Moumei exceeded the principle of privity in insurance contract disputes. Therefore, the reapplication of Wu Moulong and Li Moumei should be dismissed.

During the retrial, none of the parties submitted new evidence and had no objections to the facts found in the original trial. This Court confirms the facts found in the first and second instances.

This Court holds that this case is a dispute over an insurance contract in navigable waters. Based on the parties' reasons for reapplication and defense opinions, the focus of this case is: Whether the insurance proceeds in question should be considered as the inheritance of the deceased Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua.

I. Relevant Provisions of the Insurance Law

According to Articles 2 and 12 of the Insurance Law, insurance is divided into personal insurance and property insurance. The Insurance Law, in Chapter 2 "Insurance Contracts," Sections 2 and 3, respectively provides for personal insurance contracts and property insurance contracts. After regulating property loss insurance in the Section on Property Insurance Contracts, Articles 65 and 66 provide for matters related to liability insurance. Accordingly, property insurance can be divided into types such as property loss insurance and liability insurance.

Article 42, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law provides for three circumstances under which insurance proceeds from personal insurance are deemed inheritance upon the death of the insured. However, the Insurance Law does not contain provisions on whether insurance proceeds from property insurance, including liability insurance, can be deemed inheritance upon the death of the insured. Given that insurance proceeds from property loss insurance are essentially a substitute or continuation of the exchange value of the relevant property (the subject matter of insurance), when the subject matter of insurance is part of the insured's inheritance, the corresponding insurance proceeds are also deemed the insured's inheritance in judicial practice. It is in this context that the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Insurance Proceeds Can Be Considered as the Insured's Inheritance determined that vehicle damage insurance is property insurance, and property insurance proceeds belong to the insured's inheritance.

II. Whether the Insurance Proceeds Under the Liability Insurance Contracts in This Case Can Be Deemed Inheritance of the Deceased

According to Article 65, Paragraph 4 of the Insurance Law, liability insurance refers to insurance in which the subject matter is the insured's liability for compensation to a third party as legally owed. Although liability insurance is also a type of property insurance, there are significant differences between liability insurance and property loss insurance in terms of the subject matter. In liability insurance, when a third party dies due to an accident within the scope of insurance, whether the insurance proceeds paid by the insurer can be deemed the inheritance of that third party should be determined based on the nature of the liability for compensation borne by the insured. It cannot be simply and uniformly concluded that all insurance proceeds from liability insurance belong to the third party's inheritance merely because liability insurance is classified as property insurance. The analysis is as follows:

First, if the liability insurance is for the insured's liability for causing property loss to a third party, the insurance proceeds paid by the insurer are in substance a substitute or continuation of the value of the damaged property owned by the third party. According to the foregoing analysis, such insurance proceeds should be deemed the inheritance of the third party. For example, payments under the "Property Loss Compensation Limit" in compulsory motor vehicle liability insurance fall under this category.

Second, if the liability insurance is for the insured's liability for compensation to a third party for death, including compensation for death, solatium for mental anguish, funeral expenses, etc., the insurance proceeds paid by the insurer are in substance a substitute for the compensation for death, solatium for mental anguish, and funeral expenses payable by the insured. Whether such insurance proceeds can be deemed the inheritance of the third party should be determined based on whether items such as compensation for death under tort law belong to the deceased's inheritance. (1) Regarding compensation for death. The compensation for death in tort law originates from the victim's death, and its essence is a consolation or compensation to the close relatives of the deceased for their own loss of interests, not compensation for the victim's life itself. Therefore, compensation for death does not belong to the deceased's inheritance. In this regard, the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Compensation for Air Crash Death Can Be Treated as Inheritance ( [2004] Min Yi Ta Zi No. 26) clearly determined: "Compensation for air crash death is compensation paid to the close relatives of the deceased based on the death of the deceased. The persons entitled to receive compensation for air crash death are the close relatives of the deceased, not the deceased. Therefore, compensation for air crash death should not be deemed inheritance." (2) Regarding solatium for mental anguish. Solatium for mental anguish is monetary compensation received by a victim for damage to personality interests or identity interests, or for mental suffering. Solatium for mental anguish paid due to the victim's death is compensation to the close relatives of the deceased for their own mental suffering and should not belong to the victim's inheritance. (3) Regarding funeral expenses. Funeral expenses refer to the costs incurred for burying the body of a natural person who died due to injury. Since such expenses are used for funeral arrangements, they should not be considered the deceased's inheritance. In summary, compensation for death, solatium for mental anguish, and funeral expenses should not be deemed the deceased's inheritance. Accordingly, for the insured's liability to pay the above compensation for death and other items, the insurance proceeds paid by the insurer to the close relatives of the deceased under the Insurance Law and the liability insurance contract are in substance a substitute for the above compensation items and should not be deemed the deceased's inheritance.

In this case, Yujiang Company, as the shipowner and employer, took out shipowner's liability to crew insurance and employer's liability insurance with PICC Luzhou Branch. Both contracts state that Yujiang Company is the insured, and Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua are listed in the crew and employee lists under both contracts. Article 65, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law provides: "Where an insurer is liable for damage caused by the insured under liability insurance to a third party, the insurer may directly pay insurance proceeds to that third party in accordance with laws or the contract." Accordingly, when an accident occurred involving the vessel in question and Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua died, PICC Luzhou Branch should, according to the provisions of the two liability insurance contracts, fulfill the obligation to pay insurance proceeds to the relevant entitled parties in respect of the liability Yujiang Company, as shipowner or employer, should bear. The original judgment calculated the compensation for death, solatium for mental anguish, and funeral expenses payable by Yujiang Company due to the deaths of Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua, respectively, in accordance with the compensation items specified in the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Compensation for Personal Injury. Within the liability limits set forth in the insurance contracts, it determined the liability of PICC Luzhou Branch to pay compensation. The parties raised no objections, and this Court affirms.

As previously discussed, the insurance proceeds payable by PICC Luzhou Branch are in substance a substitute for the compensation for death, solatium for mental anguish, and funeral expenses that Yujiang Company should pay, and are not part of the inheritance of Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua under the law. Therefore, whether Wu Moulong and Li Moumei have declared renunciation of their inheritance from Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua does not affect their right to claim the insurance proceeds in this case as close relatives. The original judgment, solely on the ground that liability insurance is property insurance, and by reference to the provision in the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Insurance Proceeds Can Be Considered as the Insured's Inheritance that "property insurance proceeds belong to the insured's inheritance," determined that the insurance proceeds in this case constituted the inheritance of Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua. This was an erroneous application of law, and this Court corrects it according to law.

III. Whether Wu Moulong, Li Moumei, and Li Mou Can Assert Claims Regarding the Insurance Proceeds in This Case

Article 1181, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Code provides: "Where the infringed person dies, his or her close relatives have the right to request the tortfeasor to assume tort liability." Article 1045, Paragraph 2 provides: "Spouses, parents, children, siblings, grandparents, maternal grandparents, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren are close relatives." In this case, Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua were husband and wife; Li Moumei and Li Mou are the children of Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua; Wu Moulong is the mother of Zhong Mouqun. Article 65, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law provides: "Where the insured under liability insurance causes damage to a third party and the insured's liability to the third party for compensation is determined, the insurer shall, at the request of the insured, directly pay insurance proceeds to that third party. If the insured neglects to make such a request, the third party has the right to directly request the insurer to pay insurance proceeds in respect of the portion for which it is entitled to compensation." Considering the claims of Wu Moulong, Li Moumei, and Li Mou in this lawsuit and their relationship as close relatives of the victims Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua, and also considering that Yujiang Company clearly agreed during the trial that Li Mou and other close relatives could directly claim insurance proceeds from PICC Luzhou Branch, this Court determines that Wu Moulong, Li Moumei, and Li Mou, as close relatives of Zhong Mouqun, have the right to jointly receive insurance proceeds calculated on the basis of Zhong Mouqun's compensation for death, funeral expenses, and solatium for mental anguish, totaling RMB 972,230; Li Moumei and Li Mou, as close relatives of Li Mouhua, have the right to jointly receive insurance proceeds calculated on the basis of Li Mouhua's compensation for death, funeral expenses, and solatium for mental anguish, totaling RMB 378,054.

In conclusion, the reapplication request of Wu Moulong and Li Moumei is well-founded and should be supported according to law. The original judgment's determination that the insurance proceeds in this case constituted the inheritance of Zhong Mouqun and Li Mouhua involved an erroneous application of law, which this Court corrects according to law. Pursuant to Article 1181 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, Article 65 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 218, Paragraph 1 and Article 177, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2023) E Min Zhong No. 296 of the Hubei High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2022) E 72 Min Chu No. 743 of the Wuhan Maritime Court;

2. People's Insurance Company of China, Luzhou Branch shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay insurance proceeds of RMB 972,230 in a lump sum to Wu Moulong, Li Moumei, and Li Mou;

3. People's Insurance Company of China, Luzhou Branch shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay insurance proceeds of RMB 378,054 in a lump sum to Li Moumei and Li Mou;

4. Dismiss the other claims of Wu Moulong, Li Moumei, and Li Mou.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 264 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 24,400, and the second-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 16,953, totaling RMB 41,353. Wu Moulong, Li Moumei, and Li Mou shall bear RMB 9,424, and People's Insurance Company of China, Luzhou Branch shall bear RMB 31,929.

This judgment is final.
